project.title: Investment Committee Simulation
project.subtitle: Three approval gates. Four committee members. One integrated recommendation.
project.premise: Your four-person investment committee advises three client mandates and manages $500,000 in hypothetical assets. The committee must establish a market view, build and challenge each portfolio, and defend one evidence-linked recommendation.
project.scopeNote: Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission links, and course-grade weights.

roles.title: Committee Chair & Client Mandate Lead
roles.mandate: Own the meeting process, client suitability, decision record, and integration across all three phases.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Lead the RRTTLLU review, resolve client constraint conflicts, and frame the approval motion.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Test whether proposed allocations and securities stay inside each approved mandate.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Open the committee meeting, state the recommendation, record the vote, and close with actions.

roles.title: Markets & Economic Strategist
roles.mandate: Own the 12-month macro thesis, scenario probabilities, data provenance, and transmission logic.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Build the human-first macro read, compare it with consensus, and propose base and bear scenarios.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Translate the approved thesis into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and macro filters.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend the market view and explain why the recommendation should work under the base case.

roles.title: Portfolio Construction Lead
roles.mandate: Own capital-market expectations, optimization, security selection, allocation, and implementation feasibility.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Identify the portfolio decisions that the approved market view and client mandates must support.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Run the CME and Solver work, select securities, document weights, and propose implementation trades.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Defend portfolio construction, security-level choices, and the path from evidence to weights.

roles.title: Risk, Controls & Challenge Lead
roles.mandate: Own independent challenge, stress testing, hedge analysis, the AI audit, and mandate-breach escalation.

phaseResponsibilities.phase-1: Challenge scenario assumptions, verify sources, and define the evidence required at the first gate.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-2: Run the bear-case stress test, compare hedges, identify breaches, and require corrective action.
phaseResponsibilities.phase-3: Present the strongest downside case and lead preparation for adversarial Q&A.

committeeProtocol.description: Circulate the required evidence before the meeting. Every member reviews the full package.
The workstream lead states a clear recommendation and cites the evidence that supports it.
The Risk, Controls & Challenge Lead presents the strongest counterargument or mandate risk.
The Chair records approve, revise, or reject. All four members vote; ties require revision.
Capture evidence reviewed, dissent or reservations, owners, and actions before the next gate.

phases.title: Frame the Mandate
phases.tagline: Agree on the world you are investing in and the rules you cannot break.
phases.keyQuestion: What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?
phases.objective: Establish one defensible 12-month market view and convert each assigned client profile into an approved investment mandate.
phases.gate: Approve or revise the common market view and all three client mandates. Portfolio construction cannot begin until the vote and action items are recorded.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the committee's market view and the investment mandate for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: Market view
workstreams.description: Read the historical data before using AI, compare the committee view with FactSet/FRED consensus, and build bull/base/bear scenarios.

workstreams.title: Client mandate
workstreams.description: Translate each client profile into RRTTLLU constraints, return targets, liquidity needs, and an explicit drawdown tripwire.

workstreams.title: Conflict register
workstreams.description: Surface tensions among return, risk, liquidity, taxes, legal restrictions, and unique circumstances before approving the mandate.

evidence: Human-first five-year macro read with source dates
FactSet/FRED consensus comparison and team forecast
Bull/base/bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%
RRTTLLU analysis for all three assigned clients
Return target, maximum volatility, and drawdown tripwire for each client
Phase 1 decision record signed by all four members

phases.title: Build & Challenge
phases.tagline: Turn the approved view into portfolios, then try to break them.
phases.keyQuestion: Does each portfolio earn its place inside the client mandate after costs, constraints, and the bear case?
phases.objective: Translate the Phase 1 view into capital-market expectations, construct client portfolios, select securities, design risk mitigation, and challenge each recommendation under stress.
phases.gate: Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. A failed tripwire cannot receive approval without a documented correction.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to approve the proposed portfolio and risk-mitigation plan for each assigned client.

workstreams.title: A · Capital-market expectations
workstreams.description: Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

workstreams.title: B · Securities & implementation
workstreams.description: Select and weight securities, document macro and client fit, and compare at least two risk-mitigation approaches.

workstreams.title: C · Stress test & corrective action
workstreams.description: Run the bear case, test the tripwire, quantify hedge effects, and document trades required to cure any breach.

evidence: Base and bear CME inputs with cited rationale
Solver output and constraint checks for each client
Security-selection table with macro connection, client fit, weight, and source
Risk-mitigation comparison showing cost and trade-offs
Stress-test result against each approved tripwire
Before/after record for any corrective trades
AI audit entries linked to human verification
Phase 2 decision record signed by all four members
deliverables: Phase 2 decision record with client-by-client votes

phases.title: Defend the Recommendation
phases.tagline: Make the recommendation visible, auditable, and defensible under pressure.
phases.keyQuestion: Can every committee member defend the same evidence-linked recommendation to the panel?
phases.objective: Integrate the committee's work into a concise decision package and defend the client recommendations before an investment-committee panel.
phases.gate: Issue the final recommendation, record dissent or reservations, and defend the evidence. Every member must answer questions outside the workstream they led.
phases.meetingMotion: Motion to issue the committee's final recommendation and implementation plan for all assigned clients.

workstreams.title: Decision memo
workstreams.description: State the recommendation first, then connect the market view, client mandate, portfolio, and risk decision.

workstreams.title: Technical exhibit book
workstreams.description: Present the auditable evidence: scenarios, IPS constraints, allocations, securities, stress results, and sources.

workstreams.title: Committee defense
workstreams.description: Deliver a visual pitch, answer adversarial questions, and show that all four members understand the integrated decision.

evidence: Executive recommendation and decision memo
Technical exhibit book linking macro, mandate, allocation, securities, and risk
Client-specific recommendation for all three assigned clients
Final decision record with vote, reservations, and implementation actions
Visual oral presentation with balanced speaking time
Cross-functional Q&A preparation
deliverables: Final decision record and AI audit appendix

resources.label: CME technical reference

resources.label: Stress-test technical reference

aiRules.title: Logic, debugging & challenge
aiRules.description: Use AI to explain formulas, test reasoning, generate counterarguments, or surface missing risks.

aiRules.title: Summaries, scenarios & estimates
aiRules.description: Cross-check every factual claim and number against FactSet, FRED, SEC filings, or the team's workbook.

aiRules.title: Unverified decisions
aiRules.description: Do not submit AI-generated allocations, risk metrics, citations, or client recommendations without human verification.

assessment.note: Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and the project's course-grade weight. The criteria below preserve the existing written/oral assessment emphasis while aligning it to Phase 3.

writtenCriteria.standard: Calculations, formulas, sources, and portfolio metrics are correct, traceable, and interpreted.
The market view visibly drives CME assumptions, portfolio weights, securities, and client recommendations.
Each portfolio is tested against its tripwire; breaches trigger documented corrective action.
Exhibits communicate the decision clearly and include complete sources and the AI audit.
RRTTLLU constraints change the actual portfolio rather than appearing as generic narrative.

oralCriteria.standard: The committee tells one coherent story from market view to client action.
Members defend the base case, bear case, trade-offs, and quantitative evidence under questioning.
The team speaks as advisors to the committee with confident, concise, client-aware language.
All four members contribute, transition cleanly, and can answer beyond their lead workstream.
Slides make the recommendation and key evidence visible at a glance rather than serving as a script.
